current_activity: first sizable US unit to drop: about half lands on the zone south-east of Le Muy, part near Saint-Tropez
notes: Event date: 15 August 1944, 0430 (Clarke and Smith, ch. 6, p. 100). Event definition: The battalion and the 463rd Parachute Field Artillery Battalion drop first; two companies land on the correct zone about two miles south-east of Le Muy at 0430, one company far off in the hills south of Saint-Tropez; that evening its troops meet a 45th Division patrol south of Le Muy (Clarke and Smith, chs. 6-7). Event support: two source families (the US Army official history (CMH), and Wikipedia). Clarke and Smith, Riviera to the Rhine, ch. 6, p. 101: "In toto, only about half the 509th's battalion combat team landed in or close to its proper drop zone"; Wikipedia, 509th Parachute Infantry Battalion: "A second combat jump, on 15 August 1944, occurred around Le Muy and St Tropez in southern France". Location: Le Muy, Var (new place) with a precision of 10 km. Location approximate: the point is Le Muy; the zone was two miles south-east of it and part of the battalion came down near Saint-Tropez, so the precision is 10 km. Location support: Clarke and Smith place the zone about two miles south-east of Le Muy. Relationship: attached with no standing parent: the sources read give no assignment of this separate unit to a corps or army for the period, so only the attachment is recorded (Brigades Batch 2).

location_qualifier: part of the battalion, with the 550th Glider Infantry Battalion
current_activity: with the 550th Glider Infantry, attacks and takes Le Muy
notes: Event date: 16 August 1944, from 0200 (Clarke and Smith, ch. 7). Event definition: The 550th Glider Infantry Battalion, supported by part of the 509th, attacks Le Muy at 0200 on 16 August, withdraws at daylight, returns at 0900 with artillery support and takes the town (Clarke and Smith, ch. 7). Event support: one source family (the US Army official history (CMH)). Clarke and Smith, Riviera to the Rhine, ch. 7, p. 118: "the 550th Glider Infantry Battalion, supported by part of the 509th Parachute Battalion, undertook the task shortly after midnight on 16 August". Location: Le Muy, Var (new place) with a precision of 3 km. Location support: Clarke and Smith name Le Muy. Relationship: attached with no standing parent: the sources read give no assignment of this separate unit to a corps or army for the period, so only the attachment is recorded (Brigades Batch 2).

current_activity: newly arrived with the 3rd Armored Division for its drive towards the Salmchâteau-La Roche road
notes: Event date: 23 December 1944 (Cole, ch. 16: the mission on the 23d). Event definition: The 3rd Armored Division's combat command has the mission on 23 December of building a line along the Salmchâteau-La Roche road; newly arrived reinforcements include the battalion (Cole, ch. 16); its Company C later holds a strongpoint north of Baraque de Fraiture with Task Force Brewster (Cole, ch. 16). Event support: one source family (the US Army official history (CMH)). Cole, The Ardennes, ch. 16, p. 385: "the 1st Battalion of the 517th Parachute Infantry and the 509th Parachute Infantry Battalion"; Cole, The Ardennes, ch. 16, p. 392: "There he placed Company C of the 509th Parachute Infantry Battalion". Location: Manhay, Luxembourg (Belgium) (new place), a representative point with a precision of 10 km. Location approximate: representative point (inferred value): Manhay, in the middle of the 3rd Armored Division sector; Cole does not place the battalion as a whole, so the precision is 10 km. Location support: Cole names the division's sector between the Soy-Hotton road and the Salmchâteau-La Roche road. Relationship: attached with no standing parent: the sources read give no assignment of this separate unit to a corps or army for the period, so only the attachment is recorded (Brigades Batch 2).

current_activity: envelops Sadzot from west and east and traps the Germans inside by 1100
notes: Event date: 28 December 1944 (Cole, ch. 23). Event definition: Germans infiltrating between two battalions of the 289th Infantry strike Sadzot in the early hours of 28 December; General Hickey sends the battalion from near Erezée to envelop the village, and by 1100 it has closed the trap (Cole, ch. 23). Event support: two source families (the US Army official history (CMH), and Wikipedia). Cole, The Ardennes, ch. 23, p. 602: "General Hickey immediately alerted the 509th Parachute Infantry Battalion near Erezée to make an envelopment of Sadzot from west and east"; Cole, The Ardennes, ch. 23, p. 602: "By 1100 the 509th had clicked the trap shut on the Germans inside Sadzot"; Wikipedia, 509th Parachute Infantry Battalion: "During the Battle of the Bulge in late 1944, the 509th fought in Belgium to blunt the German attack". Location: Sadzot, Luxembourg (Belgium) (new place) with a precision of 3 km. Location support: Cole names Sadzot. Relationship: attached with no standing parent: the sources read give no assignment of this separate unit to a corps or army for the period, so only the attachment is recorded (Brigades Batch 2).
